pairs.question: Quae potest antiquior forma proferri quam ipse census generis humani?
pairs.answer: Unam feminam masculo deus finxit una costa eius decerpta et utique ex pluribus.
pairs.derivation: Authorial-rhetorical: Tertullian asks what more ancient form (of monogamy) could be adduced than the origin of the human race, and answers himself in the next sentence. Stripped the section marker '[2]' and the preceding clause 'Quod pertineat ad antiquitatem,' which frames the topic but is not part of the question. Answer ends at the first full stop ('ex pluribus.'); what follows ('Sed et in praefatione ipsius operis...') turns to a further scriptural proof.

pairs.question: Quae ista materia apostolo fuit scribendi talia?
pairs.answer: Tirocinium novae et quam maxime orientis ecclesiae, quam lacte scilicet educabat, nondum solido cibo validioris doctrinae, adeo ut prae illa infantia fidei ignorarent adhuc, quid sibi agendum esset circa carnis et sexus necessitatem.
pairs.derivation: Authorial-rhetorical: Tertullian asks what the apostle's subject-matter (materia) was in writing such things, and answers himself with the nominal phrase beginning 'Tirocinium novae... ecclesiae'. Stripped section marker '[9]' and the lead-in 'Eam rationem in ipsa materia poterimus recognoscere.' which precedes the question. Answer runs to the first full stop ('necessitatem.'); the next sentence '[10] Cuius etiam ipsas species ex rescriptis intelligimus...' begins elaboration.
